subject: Cognitive Science
title: Decision Hygiene
description: A short lesson to help you apply Decision Hygiene.

hook.text: Two judges sentence differently for the same crime depending on whether it's before or after lunch.

buildup.text: Kahneman's "decision hygiene" applies noise reduction to judgment: structure processes to cut variability.

discovery.text: Noise is random error: different judges, different days, different moods produce different decisions on the same case.

twist.text: Noise is as damaging as bias but gets far less attention. We fix bias and ignore the randomness.

climax.text: Structured interviews, checklists, and independent evaluations are proven noise-reducers that anyone can use.

punchline.text: Good process matters more than good intentions.

quiz.question: What is noise in decision-making?
options: Random variability in judgments on the same case
